primary_objective: tree structural entropy H^T; lower is better

claims.claim: The weighted rooted-NNI delta equals the two-cross-weight closed form.
claims.evidence: Random weighted graphs and binary trees; compare every predicted delta with full H^T recomputation.
claims.falsifier: Any mismatch above 1e-9 after ruling out floating-point accumulation.

claims.claim: se_hier_nni never worsens H^T relative to the identical se_hier initializer.
claims.evidence: Per-run paired H^T records and monotonic move traces.
claims.falsifier: Any final H^T greater than its paired initializer beyond 1e-10.

claims.claim: NNI closes a reproducible local-optimality gap left by current hierarchy constructors.
claims.evidence: Paired refinement of se_hier, HCSE, BBM, Paris, and agglomerative outputs over held-out seeds.
claims.falsifier: Improvements occur only on development graphs or only on a hand-built clique.

claims.claim: Bounded compound NNI escapes cases where strict one-NNI descent stalls.
claims.evidence: Exact trap family plus naturally occurring held-out one-NNI local optima.
claims.falsifier: Compound search adds cost without improving any non-constructed case.

claims.claim: The enhanced optimizer improves the practical entropy/runtime frontier.
claims.evidence: H^T, hierarchy recovery, runtime, and peak RAM with 95% confidence intervals.
claims.falsifier: Lower H^T requires prohibitive runtime or degrades hierarchy recovery consistently.

held_out: hierarchical SBM with depth, imbalance, and noise sweeps
real graphs with usable hierarchy or taxonomy labels

statistics: Paired per-seed comparisons; report mean, 95% confidence interval, and raw records.
